summary: This is a sound stage-1 rewrite that goes after the part of sliding-layer time that is launches and latency. The profile shows 15-27 us of replaced GPU time spread over 5 launches to move 0.5-16.8 MB. The only landed hypothesis is absorbed by this change on sliding layers and left byte-identical on full layers, so one run is interpretable from the single kernel's profile line with full layers as the drift control. No companions are needed.
justification: Mechanism: on sliding shapes FA3 main (7.7-14.9 us), FlashAttnFwdCombine (2.5-4.3 us), prepare_varlen_num_blocks (1.8 us), _pre_attention_kernel (1.5-4.1 us) and rms_norm_gate (~1 us) cost 15-27 us. The bytes moved are 512 KB at B=1 (2048 keys x 2 kv heads x 128 B K+V) and 8.4/16.8 MB at B=16/32, against floors of 0.1/1.6/3.3 us. So the time is dependent launches and DRAM latency, not bandwidth. LESSONS records the one place fusion paid: launch-dominated 17-36 us attention_decode shapes (1.127x). The expected directions fit the weights. Sliding shapes carry weight 46 against 16 for full, so sliding is ~63% of load time at B=1 (46*16.8 vs 16*27.9) and ~16-24% at B=16/32. The large geomean lever is therefore decode_1/verify_1. The full-layer 'flat' row is correct: that path is byte-identical. Window algebra checks out against FA3 window_size (window-1, 0). lo = seq-(window-1) is the j=0 lower bound and so the union over the block. The old-key mask t >= p_j-window+1 and the new-key mask i <= j reproduce causal-in-block, and the dist=edges keys at p0-2047 (in for j=0, out for j>=1) and p0-2048 (out) fall on the right side. Attending the E4M3-rounded new k/v from registers matches the judge, which attends your own new entries, and avoids a store-then-load race. Feeding bf16 queries is finer than the E4M3 allowance. Weakest link: the B=1/verify_1 critical path is a dependent chain, and the per-shape targets are optimistic. The chain is cold qkv + page_table load -> row-index gather of K/V -> partial store -> gpu-scope atomic ticket -> winner re-reads S partials -> gate load -> store, inside one launch. That is realistically ~5-8 us, not <=6 us. At B=32 LESSONS measured the page-size-1 row gather at 1.3-1.7 TB/s, which puts 16.8 MB at ~10-13 us, not <=9. Both still clear the incumbent's 15-27 us replaced time by a wide margin, so milestone 2 (beat the incumbent) is very likely, but 'within 1.5x the floor' (milestone 3) is unreachable at B=1 (floor 0.1 us) for any design. Judge stage 1 on replaced time vs incumbent, not on the floor ratio. The second risk is the Triton ticket combine's memory ordering: release by one thread after tl.debug_barrier. Make it robust before trusting a pass on its own; see open_questions.
confounders: fused-preattention-triton (landed, master base): not a confounder for the sliding rows. This change removes _pre_attention_kernel from the sliding path and re-does its work (q/k RMSNorm+RoPE, k/v E4M3 store at cache_loc) inside the new kernel, so a sliding gain or loss belongs to the new kernel and not to an interaction. Its only residual effect is that the incumbent being compared against is 1.5-4.1 us cheaper than SGLang's 5-launch pre-attention. That makes the measured gain a lower bound of the gain against SGLang, not an inflated one. On full layers it stays byte-for-byte, which makes the full rows a same-run drift control.
interference: No companion is warranted. (i) An ab-revert of fused-preattention-triton is meaningless on sliding layers because the change subsumes that kernel there, and it would only perturb the full-layer control. (ii) There is no landed knob to tune that the new kernel depends on. (iii) A control isolating a sub-change, such as S=1 with no in-kernel combine, or keeping rms_norm_gate separate, is not needed to read this result. The profile gives the single kernel's own time per sliding shape against the 15-27 us replaced sum, the full-layer rows bound run-to-run drift (~1.5-2.5%), and the expected effect (several us on 17-29 us shapes) is far above noise. Both a gain and a loss are attributable to the new kernel. If B=1 disappoints, the S=1 fallback and a raised S are next-stage material, not companions, as the rewrite rules prescribe.
rules_flags: Persistent zeroed int32 ticket counters, allocated once per (B, Hkv, device) before capture and reset to 0 by the winning program: this is config-shaped workspace that holds no input-derived data between calls, so I read it as not violating 'don't cache anything derived from data'. Two conditions: the counters must be keyed only on config/device, and the reset must run on every S>1 path, and with S=1 the counters must not be touched at all. decode_1 and verify_1 share B=1 and so share one buffer. That is safe only because graph replays on one stream serialize, so do not launch the new kernel on a side stream.

Every key: each token's full 2048-token window is scored (old keys [p_j-2047, seq-1] plus new keys i<=j). Empty chunks are allowed only for short contexts. No skipping by score: compliant. Keep it that way at stage 2 (no early-out on m).

Precision: bf16 queries are finer than the E4M3 allowance. bf16 P in P@V is finer than FA3's FP8 P. fp32 o before the output norm is finer than SGLang's bf16 round. The KV cache stays E4M3. Compliant. If E4M3 x E4M3 tl.dot is chosen for QK^T it is also allowed, but record which one, as the hypothesis says.

No host syncs or value-dependent branching: all branches are on config (batch, q_len, page_size, window). The workspace is torch.empty with a config-only shape, which is fine under graph capture. The _inv_freq cache is keyed on config theta and is already on master: fine.
open_questions: Ticket-combine ordering in Triton: a scalar tl.atomic_add(sem='acq_rel') is issued by one thread after tl.debug_barrier. Is that cumulative over the other threads' partial stores on sm_90 as Triton lowers it? The conservative CUDA pattern is a gpu-scope fence by every thread, then the barrier, then the atomic, then an acquire on the winner side. Validate it with a stress loop of many replays at B=1 and S=16 locally before the run. A sporadic mis-combine would surface as a flaky correctness failure on a timed call, not on the tests.

Online-softmax -inf guard: rows can be fully masked inside a block, for example verify rows j>=1 at the window's lower edge or tail blocks past seq-1. m_new must stay -inf-safe (exp2(-inf - -inf) = NaN), and the combine must use m_max from finite partials. The S-1 partial is always finite because it holds the new keys, but the winner may be any program. Check this explicitly. The 'No NaN or Inf' rule fails the whole run.

Does the S-1 program's extra prologue (building, storing and attending L new k/v rows) lengthen the critical path at B=1, given that it also runs the main loop over a full chunk? Consider giving chunk S-1 fewer old keys or none, so its new-key work overlaps the others' gathers.

Milestone 3 (within ~1.5x of the floor) cannot be met at B=1/verify_1, where the floor is 0.1 us after the judge's ~4 us fixed-cost subtraction. Churnsubs should judge stage 1 on M1/M2 and on whether B=16/32 approach the page-1 gather ceiling (~1.3-1.7 TB/s per LESSONS), and not treat a missed M3 at B=1 as a failure.

If this lands, the queued sliding-only FA3 hypotheses become moot for sliding layers: triton-window-attention-sliding, fused-sliding-preattn-into-window-kernel, fused-sliding-normgate-epilogue, fa3-single-split-sliding, fa3-window-trimmed-page-table and fa3-num-splits-sliding. Churnsubs should park them rather than run them against the new base.
